sections.h2: Richland County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Columbia, the state capital, anchors Richland County in the Midlands as its seat and largest community. Around it sit Cayce, Forest Acres, Arcadia Lakes, Blythewood, Eastover, Elgin and Irmo. The county had 416,147 residents in 2020, and health care leads local employment with 15.3% of jobs.

Whether a parcel lies in Eastover, Blythewood, Irmo or Columbia, one county Treasurer bills it. Typical sellers own an inherited house, a rental behind on tax or a home in poor shape, and each situation calls for its own tax step before closing.

sections.h2: Where to pay and who to call
sections.html:
OfficeLocation and hoursContact
Treasurer2020 Hampton Street, Columbia, SC 29204; 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday803-576-2250; treasurer@richlandcountysc.gov
Assessor2020 Hampton Street, Suite 2058, Columbia, SC 29204; mail to P.O. Box 192, Columbia, SC 29202803-576-2640; assessoroffice@richlandcountysc.gov

Payment is accepted online, at the counter or through the mail, and a monthly plan is available. Customer service, planned payments and tax sale questions each have their own Treasurer email address.

The penalty-free window closes January 15 (S.C. Code 12-45-70). Late charges under 12-45-180 then run 3%, followed by 7% more ahead of February 2 and 5% more ahead of March 17.

Penalties are waived when ownership changed during the tax year and the buyer never received the notice on time. If your closing fits that pattern, say so to the Treasurer's office.

Each fall the county auctions delinquent parcels by sealed bid at the Richland County Township Auditorium, 1703 Taylor Street, Columbia. The top bidder gets the property as is, paying cash. An owner who wants a parcel pulled must get cash or a certified cashier's check to the Treasurer by the announced cutoff. Personal, company and escrow checks don't count.

  • Registration for bidders is online only and costs $50.00.
  • Bidding opens at the sum of delinquent taxes, sale costs and current year taxes.
  • A winner who doesn't pay owes $500 per bid and court costs.
  • Title passes without warranty, and the county may cancel a sale before the deed issues.

Because the schedule changes yearly, ask the Treasurer for current dates.

Every five years the Assessor revalues the whole county, following S.C. Code 12-43-217. The next year is a question for 803-576-2640. Notice is owed when a value or classification shifts by $1,000 or more, and an ordinance can hold off new values for one tax year at most.

Beyond values, that office deals with rollback taxes on farmland that changes use, HOA properties, active military residential exemptions and deed sale records. Multiple-lot and builder or developer discounts, commercial ATI exemptions and mailing address changes are on its list as well, so let it know when you sell or move.

Your written objection must reach the Assessor within 90 days of the date on the reassessment notice. In a year with no notice, the first penalty date on the tax bill is the cutoff. Online filers follow whichever date comes first.

  1. Go through the county's Appeal Your Assessment portal, or write a letter.
  2. Attach papers that challenge the assessed value or classification.
  3. A representative filing on your behalf needs a power of attorney on SC DOR Form SC2848.
  4. An LLC or similar owner adds its Articles of Organization or Operating Agreement.

Disputes between taxpayer and Assessor go to a Board of Assessment Appeals. Paper filings can be sent to the Assessor's street address or P.O. Box.

A home that meets the residency and ownership tests drops from the 6% ratio to 4%. The rate under S.C. Code 12-43-220 reaches the house and as many as five contiguous acres, and leasing the house more than 72 days in a calendar year forfeits it.

Anyone who loses eligibility and keeps quiet past six months risks a charge equal to the tax paid, plus 0.5% interest monthly, with a floor of $30.

Landlords and heirs who live elsewhere should plan on 6%. The same section treats active-duty residents with South Carolina duty stations as domiciled here.

Begin with a payoff number from the Treasurer so you know what will leave your proceeds. Closing pays the tax, and Cash Home Buyers will purchase the house in its present state, repairs not required.

  • Treasurer, 803-576-2250: current bill and tax sale questions.
  • Assessor, 803-576-2640: rate, value and appeals.
  • Deed recording: $1.85 per $500 of value, split $1.30 state and $0.55 county (S.C. Code 12-24-10), with deeds in lieu of foreclosure exempt.

Cash also avoids the lender appraisal and a buyer's repair list, which fits a house in poor condition or an estate in a hurry.

Short of cash on January 15? Ask the Treasurer about the monthly plan. It spreads out the payments without protecting you: until the full amount is in, penalties and collection steps can continue. Think of it as a bridge to a sale more than a way to keep a house you can't afford.

Selling while on a plan? Tell the title company up front. The payoff is the leftover balance plus any penalties that have built up, and the Treasurer can supply it. The planned-payments email address works for written questions about your account.

sections.h2: A sensible order for a quick sale
sections.html:
First, the Treasurer: confirm the balance, which years are open and whether the parcel is headed for the fall sale. Second, the Assessor: which rate applies and whether a reassessment is near. Third, pass both answers to the title company with your target closing date.

A closing ahead of the fall sale keeps the property out of the auction altogether. Auction buyers get title without warranty and the county can cancel a sale, so no owner should count on that route. Selling first is cleaner.

Keep a written record of every call. Note the date, the person you spoke with and the figure you were given, since payoff amounts change as penalty dates pass and you may need to show where a number came from.

Photo ID and the property address are the basics at the Hampton Street office. Executors and agents should add proof of authority, and an LLC owner should have its founding papers handy.

An inherited house may hold several years of tax and a classification that no longer fits. Heirs who live elsewhere face the 6% rate, and the balance may include old penalties. Ask the Treasurer for a full payoff and set it beside what a buyer will pay.

Landlords with a rental in arrears face the same arithmetic. Tax is paid from the proceeds, so the question is whether the price covers the balance with margin. A cash buyer can quote a number fast, since no lender appraisal is involved.

faqs.q: What is the Richland County tax deadline?
faqs.a: Pay by January 15 to avoid penalties. A 3% charge starts after that date.

faqs.q: Where is the Richland County Treasurer?
faqs.a: At 2020 Hampton Street, Columbia, SC 29204. Call 803-576-2250 during weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Richland County assessment?
faqs.a: Write to the Assessor within 90 days of the reassessment notice, or use the online portal. Someone filing for you needs Form SC2848.

faqs.q: Can I pay Richland County tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Treasurer's monthly plan, though collection steps go on until the full amount is paid.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Richland County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing pays the tax from your proceeds, and Cash Home Buyers can buy the house in its current condition.
